The heart of it

What is “2 Fish”?

You’ve heard the old proverb: give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime. At MannaFish we read it through the eyes of the One who fed the thousands.

In John 6, a boy brings five loaves and two small fishes — an ordinary lunch — and places it in Jesus’ hands. Blessed and broken, it feeds a multitude, with baskets left over. That’s the “2 Fish.”

Two fish means one for me, and one for you. First I take the Word and apply it to my own life. Then I give it away — and I teach the next person to do the same. A meal becomes a multiplication.

“There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?”John 6:9 · KJV

It’s the pattern of the manna in the wilderness: gather enough for yourself, and enough for those who cannot yet gather for themselves. Nobody goes without, and everybody learns to gather.

And here is the freedom in it — we are laborers together. One plants, another waters, but God gives the increase. That takes the pressure off, and puts the glory where it belongs.

What the name means
Manna — “What is it?”

Bread from heaven.

When bread appeared in the wilderness, Israel asked “man hu?” — “what is it?” That very question became its name: manna. It fell fresh each morning, enough for the day — God’s daily provision from heaven (Exodus 16).

Centuries later, Jesus said, “I am the bread of life … the living bread which came down from heaven.” The manna was a picture; He is the true Bread. And His Word is our manna — daily, from heaven, gathered fresh.

“I am that bread of life.” · John 6:48
The Fish — a hidden confession

Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.

The early church, under persecution, drew a simple fish to know one another. Its Greek name, ΙΧΘΥΣ (ichthys), spelled a whole creed: Iēsous Christos, Theou Huios, Sōtēr — “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.”

One quiet line said everything. And it echoes His call to the first disciples — ordinary fishermen — “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.”

“… I will make you fishers of men.” · Matthew 4:19
MannaFish

Put the two together and you have the whole purpose: the Bread of the Word, carried on the sign of the Fish. We take one word of God — your manna for today — and place it in your hands on the fish that confesses Him. Then we teach you to hand one to the next person. It all lives in a single chapter, John 6 — where five loaves and two small fishes fed a multitude, and Jesus called Himself the Bread from heaven.
